ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior managers against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the People's Bank of China (PBOC) domestic sanctions and PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence is required for any individual identified as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or with any adverse media or negative news. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a continuous basis (at least quarterly), and upon any material change in ownership or control. All results must be documented and retained for at least five years. For this low-risk data labeling BPO, standard due diligence applies, but any PEP or sanctions hit triggers immediate escalation to the AML compliance officer and potential rejection of the engagement.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Registration and Clearance System (via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Chinese characters, following the four-tier structure: administrative division (e.g., 'Shanghai'), trade name (unique and not identical or confusingly similar to existing names), industry description (e.g., 'Data Labeling'), and organizational form (e.g., 'Co., Ltd.'). For foreign investors, the trade name may be a phonetic transliteration (pinyin) of the foreign name, but must be approved by SAMR. English names are not registered but may be used for business purposes; however, the Chinese name is the legal name.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), particularly Articles 5, 6, 7, 9, 14, 23-36, 42-57, 63-75, 76-90, 91-105, 106-133, 134-188, 189-215 and 232; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019, effective 1 January 2020), Articles 2, 4, 5, 9, 12, 28, 30 and 31; Regulations on Implementing the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (State Council Order No. 723)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local Municipal or Provincial Administration for Market Regulation, Enterprise Registration Division, acting through the National Enterprise Registration Online Service System
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, together with the signed Articles of Association, submitted via the SAMR National Enterprise Registration Online Service System
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. There is no statutory minimum registered capital or blocked escrow account requirement for an ordinary service-sector WFOE engaged in AI data labeling and BPO. The registered capital shall be stated in the Articles of Association and must be fully paid by all shareholders within five years from incorporation under the 2023 Company Law, unless a shorter contribution period is adopted in the Articles. Foreign exchange contributions must be remitted through a designated bank and reported under the State Administration of Foreign Exchange foreign direct investment registration procedure.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION NO. 2025-001
FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN WFOE LTD
(WHOLLY FOREIGN-OWNED ENTERPRISE, LIMITED LIABILITY)

WHEREAS: A. The Company was organized as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China. B. The Board of Directors is lawfully constituted and authorized to adopt initial corporate governance and formation resolutions. C. The Board has reviewed the draft Articles of Association, the registered capital commitment of the foreign shareholder, the proposed registered office, and the candidates for statutory officers.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. RESOLVED, that the registered capital of the Company be fixed at RMB [amount], divided into [number] equity interests of RMB [amount] each, and that such registered capital be subscribed by the foreign shareholder as set forth in the Articles of Association. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the entire registered capital be paid in cash from lawful foreign exchange sources in accordance with the Foreign Investment Law and the contribution schedule approved by the shareholder; that the legal representative shall open a foreign exchange capital account with the designated bank; and that each contribution shall be remitted, reported, and settled in compliance with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange. RESOLVED FURTHER, that no certificate of capital contribution shall be issued until consideration is fully received.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the Company adopt [Bank Name] as its principal banker, and that the Board and the General Manager are authorized to open a basic deposit account, general deposit account, foreign exchange settlement account, and such other accounts as may be necessary. RESOLVED FURTHER, that any two authorized signatories, one being the legal representative or General Manager and the other being the Finance Officer, shall jointly execute banking instructions, loan documents, guarantees, and electronic banking mandates, and that a specimen signature card be maintained with the bank.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED, that the registered office and principal place of business of the Company be established at [full registered address], and that the Board is authorized to execute the lease, procure structural and fire safety certificates, and file the address with the Administration for Market Regulation. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office address shall be maintained on the business license as the statutory address for service of process and regulatory notices.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed legal representative, Chairman, and General Manager of the Company, with full authority to invest, borrow, contract, execute tax filings, sign corporate instruments, and bind the Company subject to the Articles. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be appointed supervisor, [Name] be appointed Finance Officer, [Name] be appointed Company Secretary, and [Name] be appointed Compliance Officer, each with the duties prescribed by the Company Law and the Articles. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the company seal, financial seal, and contract seal shall be kept under dual custody of the General Manager and the Company Secretary, and that no seal shall be affixed except in accordance with this resolution.

5. GENERAL AUTHORITY AND RATIFICATION. RESOLVED, that all actions taken by the promoters, legal representative, and professional advisers before the date of this resolution are ratified and confirmed. RESOLVED FURTHER, that certified copies of this resolution, certified by the Company Secretary, be delivered to the Administration for Market Regulation, the designated bank, the tax authority, and any other relevant authority. This resolution is effective immediately and shall remain in full force and effect until amended or rescinded by a subsequent board resolution.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned directors have executed this resolution on ____, 20__.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise Name Pre-Registration and Foreign Investment Negative List Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / local Market Regulation Bureau via the National Enterprise Registration Online Service System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the enterprise name pre-approval application online, selecting the foreign-invested limited liability company category. Provide at least two proposed Chinese company names and state the intended business scope precisely as artificial-intelligence data annotation, data labeling, training dataset curation, and business process outsourcing services. The filing agent must concurrently screen the Foreign Investment Access Negative List to confirm that this service activity is in the permitted or encouraged category. If the business scope raises questions concerning data services or telecom value-added services, prepare a legal memorandum and amend the scope before incorporation to avoid regulatory delay.
required_dossiers: Enterprise name pre-registration application form
Apostilled certificate of incorporation of the foreign investor
Certificate of incumbency or register of directors of the foreign investor
Power of attorney appointing the local filing agent
Passport copies of proposed directors, legal representative, and supervisor
Preliminary Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because of similarity or conflict, promptly submit two alternative names and a written explanation to the registration authority. If the business scope is suspended due to Negative List concerns, revise the scope and, if necessary, request a pre-consultation meeting or written clearance from the SAMR local foreign investment desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization, Apostille or Consular Legalization, Chinese Translation, and Foreign Exchange Capital Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public or designated authority in the home jurisdiction of the foreign investor; Chinese Embassy or Consulate where apostille is not available; licensed Chinese translation service provider; a SAFE-qualified Chinese commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain an apostille on the foreign investor's certificate of incorporation, register of directors, and parent board resolution under the Hague Apostille Convention, which became effective for China on 7 November 2023. For documents originating from non-Convention states, complete the chain of consular legalization at the Chinese embassy or consulate in the jurisdiction of issuance. Arrange certified Chinese translations, stamped and signed by the translation company, for all foreign-language documents. In parallel, instruct the foreign parent to execute a subscription resolution and a capital contribution schedule, and pre-coordinate with a designated Chinese bank to handle the foreign direct investment capital account registration under SAFE rules. No escrow or blocked capital account is required for this service WFOE.
required_dossiers: Apostilled or consularized certificate of incorporation of the foreign investor
Apostilled or consularized board resolution of the foreign investor authorizing the WFOE subscription
Certificate of good standing, if available
Passport copies of beneficial owners, directors, legal representative, and supervisor
Power of attorney for local registration
Certified Chinese translations of all foreign-language documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the apostille or legalization is rejected, correct the certificate with the issuing authority and re-submit. If the Chinese translation is queried by SAMR or the bank, obtain an affidavit or a replacement translation from a certified translator and resubmit with an explanatory cover letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SAMR Incorporation Filing and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / local Administration for Market Regulation via the government service online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the foreign-invested enterprise incorporation application on the SAMR online portal, attaching the approved name pre-registration, signed Articles of Association, certificate of office address, investor qualification documents, and appointment instruments for the legal representative, supervisor, directors, finance officer, and company secretary. The application must be electronically signed by the foreign shareholder and the first legal representative using the recognized CA-certified digital signature platform. SAMR will verify the registered capital, business scope, and statutory address; upon approval, the business license with a uniform social credit code will be issued. Immediately after license issuance, arrange engraving of the company seal, financial seal, contract seal, and legal representative seal, and begin the follow-on tax and social insurance initialization.
required_dossiers: SAMR foreign-invested enterprise registration application form
Signed Articles of Association
Enterprise name pre-approval notice
Certificate of legal representative appointment
Notice of appointment of directors, supervisor, finance officer, and company secretary
Office lease agreement and certificate of property ownership or landlord consent
Apostilled investor qualification documents with certified Chinese translations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR issues a supplementary information notice, respond within fifteen working days with corrected Articles, revised address proof, or an explanatory letter. If the application is suspended owing to address or business scope issues, request a face-to-face pre-review at the enterprise registration window and provide the requested supporting documentation in electronic and paper form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Registrations: Tax, Bank Accounts, SAFE FDI Registration, Social Insurance, and Annual Reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration local office; designated commercial bank; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through authorized banks; Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; local statistics bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within thirty calendar days after the business license date, complete tax registration and information confirmation through the local tax authority or electronic portal, apply for invoice quotas, and determine VAT status including general taxpayer eligibility. Open the basic deposit account with the selected bank, then complete foreign direct investment foreign-exchange registration through the bank, ensuring that the paid-in capital schedule matches the SAMR filings. Register all employees and the legal representative with the Human Resources and Social Security Bureau, sign labor contracts, and enroll the company in the five social insurance funds and the housing fund. Register the enterprise in the statistical basic unit database and establish the annual reporting duty through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, filing before 30 June each year.
required_dossiers: Business license with uniform social credit code
Articles of Association
Legal representative identification documents
Company seal and financial seal
Office lease contract and address proof
Bank account opening documents and notification
SAFE foreign direct investment registration form
Tax registration information form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is blocked by a missing address or identity document, complete the deficiency at the tax service hall and obtain an acceptance receipt. If SAFE or the bank questions the capital contribution schedule, provide the board resolution approving the schedule and a revised timeline, and resubmit through the bank's compliance desk.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial licensing board is required for a pure office-based AI data annotation, data labeling, and BPO service company; the only general registration authority remains the State Administration for Market Regulation
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating, manufacturing, or assembly permit is required under ISIC 8220 / NAICS 518210 for this digital services WFOE

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China - general oversight only; no project-specific authorization required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable / Exempt - office-based data labeling and BPO services are not listed in the MEE Classified Management List for Environmental Impact Assessment and therefore do not require a full EIA report, environmental registration, or pollutant discharge permit
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the operation generates no industrial wastewater, boiler emissions, regulated VOCs, or hazardous waste streams. Office waste must be sorted and disposed of under municipal solid waste rules, and electronic waste must be transferred to a licensed recycler.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as a civil-defense installation or manufacturing facility. The leased office must nevertheless maintain a valid fire safety inspection or acceptance certificate, functional emergency exits, accessible fire extinguishers, and compliance with workplace safety regulations under the Work Safety Law. If the data annotation activity requires a dedicated server room, structural load clearance shall be obtained from a qualified engineer.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) and its electronic tax administration portal, the National Electronic Tax Bureau (China e-Tax Bureau), operated through the STA's digital taxpayer services, including the China Tax Service web portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Following approval by the Ministry of Commerce and local market-regulation authority, the WFOE is incorporated with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), which issues a business license and an 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). The USCC is automatically synchronised to the STA electronic tax bureau and constitutes the statutory TIN and VAT identification number; no separate TIN application is required. The WFOE's legal representative and foreign shareholders then provide identity documentation through the National Electronic Tax Bureau to activate the entity's VAT taxpayer file, accounting profile and e-invoice eligibility. If export zero-rating is intended, the WFOE must also obtain customs registration with the General Administration of Customs (GACC) using the same USCC and complete foreign-exchange repatriation reporting arrangements with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not apply check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections. However, a WFOE may elect to be treated as a general VAT taxpayer once its annual taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5 million or, below that threshold, at its option subject to STA conditions; otherwise it remains a small-scale VAT taxpayer.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax administered under the PRC VAT Law and implementing provisional regulations; applicable rate confirmed as the service rate for modern services and data-labeling BPO suppliers)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5 million of annual taxable turnover (including services supplied by the WFOE) is the statutory threshold triggering compulsory general VAT taxpayer registration; below RMB 5 million the WFOE is registerable as a small-scale VAT taxpayer, but tax registration is nevertheless mandatory from the first taxable supply in China.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates a national real-time e-invoicing clearance regime through the STA National Electronic Invoice Service Platform. All VAT invoices issued by a WFOE must be generated as all-digital e-invoices (full-digital invoices) in the e-Tax Bureau, transmitted in real time to the tax authorities, and carry a unique invoice number and anti-counterfeiting QR/verification code. Registered enterprises integrate their billing or ERP systems with the STA through certified APIs or e-Tax application interfaces; invoice consumption, input VAT deductions and export VAT zero-rating declarations are validated on a real-time basis. Separate paper fiscal stamping is abolished in favour of the Golden Tax System phase-IV data clearance and the all-digital e-invoice anti-fraud engine.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for physical exports of goods where the WFOE is a VAT general taxpayer, the goods are exported through GACC customs procedures, the export sale is made under a foreign contract, consideration is charged in foreign currency, and the export proceeds are repatriated into China within the statutory period. For cross-border services such as data labeling, AI training data curation and RLHF BPO, zero-rating or export-deemed exemption applies only where the service is rendered to an overseas recipient and consumed wholly outside China; the WFOE must demonstrate the offshore nature through the export service contract, evidence that no concurrent domestic-use benefit is obtained, and, where applicable, inclusion in the STA catalogue of cross-border zero-rated/exempt services (including offshore outsourcing of IT and business-process services).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Goods Customs Declaration (Export Goods Declaration Form) as cleared by the General Administration of Customs
Customs-approved bill of lading or airway bill evidencing physical departure from PRC customs territory
Signed export contract and commercial invoice with the overseas buyer
Packing list and customs valuation documents if goods are exported
Bank receipt or Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by a PRC bank confirming foreign-exchange receipt from abroad

VAT export zero-rating declaration and supporting tax-audit schedule filed on the National Electronic Tax Bureau and, for services, the cross-border service export registration/declaration submitted to STA and SAFE
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If zero-rating is claimed with incomplete or inconsistent documents, STA may withdraw zero-rating and raise unpaid output VAT together with input-credit clawback, recalculated at the applicable positive rate (6% for VAT on services or 13% for goods if export status fails). Unpaid tax carries a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day from the due date until settlement. Under the PRC Tax Collection and Administration Law, fraudulent zero-rating claims are treated as tax evasion or export-rebate fraud, with administrative penalties of 50% to five times the underpaid/refunded VAT and criminal liability under the PRC Criminal Law for fraudulent export tax rebates, including imprisonment; recovery is not time-limited in cases of intentional false export declarations or forged customs/financial documents.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) acting jointly as the central foreign exchange regulator package
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a managed floating RMB exchange rate regime underpinned by current-account convertibility formalised within its Foreign Exchange Control Regulations. Revenue generated by the AI data-labeling BPO service exports is treated as current-account service-trade receipts; such receipts are freely convertible into RMB at a designated FX bank after contract, invoice, and transaction background verification. Capital-account items, including FDI equity injections into the WFOE, remain subject to SAFE registration, purpose-bound fund usage, and a separate scheme for capital-account FX positions. Profit remittance is permitted only after the firm documents audited after-tax earnings and withholds the applicable enterprise income tax for the non-resident parent-scope shareholder, evidenced by tax clearance manifests. In practice the convertibility friction appears in non-routine capital flows: cross-border shareholder loans, licence/IP royalties, and deployment of unused equity capital require additional registration or debt-modality approval. The WFOE treasury must therefore maintain a full cash-flow ledger showing that every RMB conversion and every foreign-currency receipt falls within the narrow purpose code declared to SAFE through the commercial bank. Current-account receipts have no compulsory surrender ratio, yet they must be repatriated into the bank account of the Chinese entity rather than left offshore; delaying repatriation exposes the enterprise to verification downgrades and throttled trade facilitation privileges.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Goods-trade export proceeds must be repatriated into the Chinese exporter's account within the operational benchmark of 180 days from customs declaration and may be retained in a foreign-currency account or settled into RMB at a designated bank; no mandatory conversion ratio exists since the post-2007 reform. For service-trade exports such as AI data-labeling fees, the receipt must be credited to the WFOE's domestic bank account on the contractual payment date, and while no statutory surrender percentage applies, every inward remittance must be matched against the underlying contract and verified by the bank under SAFE's current-account monitoring. Enterprises classified as Class 'A' enjoy fast-track clearance; Class 'B' and 'C' classifications impose escalated documentary verification and restrict the WFOE from producing inbound foreign currency without prior compliance approvals.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary treasury rail. The Chinese WFOE cannot be serviced by Wise or PayPal as a substitutive corporate bank account because these fintech EMIs do not hold a PBOC payment institution licence and are not authorised to receive FDI capital injections, issue RMB accounts, or perform SAFE reporting within mainland China. They may only serve as supplemental micro-disbursement rails for small foreign-currency payments to overseas annotation contractors through Mass PayPal Payout or similar channels. Any attempt to route principal current-account service receipts or equity capital through an offshore EMI would violate SAFE's current-account verification framework and expose the enterprise to administrative penalties and demotion of its FX compliance classification.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical KYC interview is mandatory. The legal representative or a locally appointed authorised signatory bearing a Company Chop, a notarised power of attorney apostilled or consularised by the Chinese embassy, and a board resolution must appear in person at the bank's operations branch. Remote video verification may be accepted only as a supplementary check and cannot replace the in-branch physical appearance. A purely consular proxy opening with no China-facing individual present is not permitted under current PBOC account-opening standards.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder structure with intermediate offshore holding companies preventing direct view of the ultimate natural persons
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate chain of title from the WFOE up to each ultimate beneficial owner with equity percentages; notarised and apostilled certificates of incorporation, register of members, and directors' resolution for every layer; scanned passports and tax-residency certificates of the ultimate individuals; an original bank reference letter from the direct parent's principal bank describing account tenure and remittance behaviour; and audited financial statements of the direct shareholder for the last two years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume recurring cross-border BPO payments that may be mischaracterised as hidden labour costs or invoicing fraud
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master service agreement and ordered task slips with overseas clients; invoice-generation log showing a unique invoice number per remittance; payroll records, work contracts, and social-insurance payment receipts for all onshore employees supporting the annotation operation; annotated screenshot dashboard showing task throughput metrics; a privacy impact assessment proving no illegal cross-border data transfer; and an English translation of the bank-declared 'Current-Account FX Income' statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party remitter or payment aggregator such as PayPal creating ambiguity about the actual obligor of the invoice
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A remittance-scheduling statement from the overseas client naming the WFOE as sole beneficiary; a contractual clause permitting third-party payer execution; a historical payment trace tying each disbursement to the corresponding invoice number; a written no-further-recourse undertaking from the third-party remitter; and the WFOE's bank-approved policy on accepting inbound payments from invoices issued to a non-remitting contracting party.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient source-of-funds evidence for the initial FDI capital injection, especially when the direct shareholder is a newly formed special purpose vehicle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SPV's audited balance sheet and bank reference letter; signed investment agreement and board resolution of the SPV parent; a sworn source-of-wealth statement for the ultimate individual investor; SAFE Foreign-Invested Enterprise Registration Code and bank-issued registration receipt; a CPA capital-verification report confirming the funds moved directly from the remitter's bank statement to the WFOE's FDI capital account; and the due-diligence file from the overseas correspondend bank that originated the credit transfer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The WFOE must first complete the FDI information registration through the designated commercial bank under SAFE. After obtaining the unique SAFE registration code, the treasury opens a foreign-currency capital account. The overseas shareholder then wires the equity amount via SWIFT MT103 using the purpose code 'Direct Investment - Paid-in Capital and Premium' and referencing the SAFE registration number on the remittance advice. Upon receipt, the bank performs a name and remittance-comparison check, converts the strict business-use portion into RMB via a capital-settlement transaction, and credits the remaining quota to a domestic RMB expenditure account for working capital. A local certified public accountant issues the capital verification report; the enterprise may use the funds only for payroll, office leasing, office equipment, cloud infrastructure, and contracted service costs. Any balance reserved for future FX conversion may be placed in a RMB capital deposit or hedged with a forward contract at the same bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the AI data-labeling BPO model, outbound disbursements are primarily vendor fees for specialised annotation platforms, overseas cloud servers, international statistics subscriptions, and independent contractor compensation. The compliant clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer after the bank verifies the service contract, proforma invoice, and completion certificate. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are only required if the WFOE later imports physical hardware such as GPU clusters; these instruments would be supported by a sales contract, transport document, and customs declaration. Dividend repatriation to the foreign parent is permitted after the enterprise income tax withholding clearance and SAFE outward-remittance form submission, accompanied by the annual or interim audit report and board-approved dividend resolution. MassPayPal Payout may be used for sub-threshold micro-payments to individual overseas crowd-workers not deemed to be employees, but cannot replace bank-mediated trade settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore FX forward contracts with genuine trade background executed through the WFOE's designated commercial bank under SAFE authorisation
FX swaps for temporal cash-flow matching between RMB expenses and foreign-currency receipts from the overseas BPO client
Plain-vanilla European-style currency options for hedging foreign-currency exposure on the WFOE's contracted cash flow

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) legally accessible only by the overseas parent or counterparties outside China; the onshore WFOE is not permitted to settle offshore NDFs as a hedger under SAFE rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Multi-Report Combined Annual Report of the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (including National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System Annual Report and Foreign Investment Information Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) in coordination with the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM), filed through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June covering the immediately preceding calendar year; no anniversary-based grace except closure of the six-month window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing places enterprise on the Operating Abnormalities List; persistent non-rectification for three consecutive years escalates to the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List; false or concealed particulars may attract administrative fines of RMB 5,000 to RMB 30,000 and ultimately trigger administrative cancellation/strike-off of the business license

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Final Settlement Return and payment of final tax balance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) through the local competent tax service bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the year following the fiscal year end for a calendar-year WFOE; within five months after the close of any approved non-calendar fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax (equivalent to 18.25% per annum); under-declaration penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax; enforced collection, freezing of bank accounts, exit restriction for the legal representative, and tax blacklisting that can trigger administrative compulsory deregistration for non-compliant dormant entities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory annual financial audit report of the WFOE prepared by an independent PRC-registered CPA firm and annual financial statements approved by the shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting and company statutory records; retained for inspection by SAMR and tax authorities where the audited report is requested or statutorily required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Latest date for completing the audit is the date on which the annual financial report is submitted for shareholder approval and used for the corporate income tax final settlement; best-practice completion before 30 April for a calendar-year WFOE, and no later than 31 May if the audited report is required for the tax filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to have the annual financial report audited in accordance with the PRC Company Law can lead administrative authorities to reject the annual report data, abnormal-listing procedures, accounting-law penalties for irregular financial reporting, and personal liability of directors and supervisors for losses caused by unlawful financial statements

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under PRC Company Law Article 164, every WFOE, irrespective of balance-sheet size, turnover, or headcount, must be independently audited by a PRC-registered CPA firm each fiscal year; no size-based exemption exists for the WFOE legal form. Additional quantitative regulatory triggers: an enterprise whose annual main-business revenue exceeds RMB 20 million is treated as an above-designated-size enterprise for statistical supervision and must reconcile its statistical financial reports to the audited statements; transfer-pricing documentation and contemporaneous file triggers apply when annual related-party tangible-asset transactions exceed RMB 200 million, financial or intangible-asset transactions exceed RMB 100 million, or other related-party services and interest transactions exceed RMB 40 million. There is no separate private-WFOE headcount trigger for statutory audit, although headcount determines payroll, social-insurance, and work-injury compliance duties.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/ASBE), substantially converged with IFRS; qualified small or micro WFOEs may apply the PRC Small Enterprise Accounting Standards for statutory reporting, but the audit report must state the applicable framework in RMB-denominated financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual multi-report confirmation filed with SAMR requires the WFOE to reconfirm ultimate beneficial owners/actual controllers, shareholders, paid-in capital, and shareholding structure. Any transfer of equity or change in shareholder/UBO must be reported to SAMR within 30 calendar days of the change; if the change has cross-border foreign-investment nature, the relevant foreign-investment information change report is required within 20 working days after the event. For anti-money-laundering bank due diligence, the WFOE must refresh its beneficial-owner confirmation with its banking partners within 30 calendar days after a change in shareholding or control.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Legal Representative and Senior Management
Register of Charges, Mortgages and Equity Pledges
Minute Book of Shareholders' Meetings and Board Meetings
Share Transfer Ledger and Capital Contribution Records
Amended Articles of Association and filed resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 to USD 2,800 per annum for a registered office/service address and a qualified local compliance agent in tier-one and tier-two cities, depending on the city and whether supplementary digital agent services are included
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800 to USD 8,500 per annum for a standard data-labeling/BPO WFOE with an ordinary bookkeeping ledger, excluding transfer-pricing documentation; larger or related-party-heavy WFOEs may incur USD 10,000 to USD 20,000 per annum

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard CIT rate is 25%. Qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises may apply a 15% rate. Small and low-profit eligible enterprises may enjoy effective rates of 5% or 10% on taxable income up to the statutory threshold. An additional 100% deduction is available for qualified R&D expenses. Certain free-trade zones such as Hainan Free Trade Port may provide a 15% rate for encouraged industries, but an AI data labeling BPO must satisfy the listed activity and revenue thresholds. Loss carryforward is 5 years generally, extended to 10 years for high-tech enterprises and technology-based SMEs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (A-Class), Form A100000, with supporting schedules including A105000 and A107000, filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing portal (eTax@China).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly provisional prepayment returns are due within 15 days after each quarter-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT reconciliation return and payment are due within five months after the fiscal year-end (May 31 for a December 31 year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenue from the AI data labeling and BPO services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize all cross-border BPO income under Chinese sourced income rules. For fees charged to overseas group companies, ensure that the amount is not artificially reduced by transfer pricing. Report all taxable revenue before intercompany adjustments; attach a related-party transaction schedule if thresholds are met.

Deduct only documented costs incurred in mainland China plus arm's length service fees. Any intercompany charges from the foreign parent must satisfy the China transfer pricing rules. Disallowed expenses include payments to shell or beneficial-owner arrangements without economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit (total profit or loss).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Start with PRC GAAP profit. Then adjust for tax recognition differences. A non-resident controlled WFOE must ensure its profit is not shifted out via excessive royalties, management fees, or service charges.

Declare all transfer pricing adjustments, thin capitalization interest disallowance, off-limits entertainment costs, and non-deductible payments. For outbound royalty or interest payments, the non-resident recipient's withholding tax treatment is reflected in the payable tax before credits.

Claim only losses that have not exceeded the five-year carryforward period (ten years for qualifying high-tech entities). The WFOE cannot use foreign losses unless under the integrated loss regime applicable to permanent establishments.

Compute final Chinese taxable income. Even if no PRC source income, a WFOE with management and control located in China is a tax resident; worldwide income may be subject to CIT unless a PE or treaty exemption applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable rate and preliminary or tentative income tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% standard rate or the applicable incentive rate. For wholly foreign-owned entities, no automatic exemption applies to dividends or profit transfers; the amount distributable to the foreign shareholder is subject to withholding tax at the time of distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits and withholding rebates, if any.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE that is a Chinese tax resident may credit foreign income taxes limited by the Chinese tax payable on the same income. For the non-resident shareholder layer, dividends paid are source-taxed in China; treaty relief must be documented at the withholding stage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party disclosures, non-resident tax withholding schedules, and tax preference schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the annual related-party transaction reporting forms if aggregate related-party transactions exceed thresholds. Report all payments to overseas connected parties subject to withholding; failure to do so triggers penalties and criminal exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties range up to RMB 10,000 under Tax Collection Administration Law Article 62; a daily late payment surcharge of 0.05% applies to unpaid tax; understatement or tax evasion carries a penalty of 50%-500% of the underpaid tax under Article 63; criminal liability arises under Criminal Law Article 201 where the evasion reaches the statutory scale threshold.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% for dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Chinese resident enterprise to its non-resident shareholder, unless reduced under an applicable Double Tax Agreement. The nominal statutory CIT rate before State Council reduction is 20%, but the effective levy is 10%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must submit to the Chinese payer or withholding agent a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty country tax authority and a Beneficial Owner self-declaration (generally SAT Form under Announcement 60/2015) prior to the dividend payment. The withholding agent applies the reduced treaty rate at source after collecting the documents; if documents cannot be provided on time, the non-resident may apply for a refund within three years through the treaty claim procedure. The recipient must have economic substance and cannot be a conduit or shell entity solely to obtain treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For interest and royalty payments to non-residents, the statutory withholding tax rate is 10%. Treaty rates vary: interest may be reduced to 5% or 0% under qualified financial institution provisions, and royalties are commonly reduced to 5%, 7%, or 10% depending on the applicable DTA. A valid TRC and beneficial ownership declaration are mandatory to obtain any treaty reduction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when annual related-party tangible or financial asset transactions exceed RMB 200 million, intangible property transactions exceed RMB 100 million, or related-party service transaction value exceeds RMB 40 million. Master File must be prepared if the MNE group's prior-year consolidated revenue exceeds RMB 2 billion and the group has Chinese related-party transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China applies substance-over-form and economic substance principles through the General Anti-Avoidance Rules and the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law. Although China does not impose Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations, treaty benefits and transfer pricing outcomes require the WFOE to show real substance: actual employees, office premises, active decision-making on AI data annotation, RLHF curation, quality control, invoicing, and IT infrastructure. Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) for the BPO are performed in mainland China; if the WFOE is a mere shell routing BPO income to an offshore entity for tax benefit, tax authorities may recharacterise the profit, deny treaty relief, and impose sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE intentionally omits AI data-labeling revenue or uses fictitious intercompany service invoices to shift profit to an overseas shell entity, thereby understating taxable income in China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Collection Administration Law Article 63: additional tax, penalty of 50%-500% of underpaid tax, and possible criminal prosecution under Criminal Law Article 201; unpaid tax plus interest is recoverable from company assets and, in fraudulent cases, from directors' personal assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who directed false invoicing or profit shifting face restitution of evaded tax from personal assets, travel restrictions or blacklisting preventing exit from China under Tax Collection Administration Law Article 44, and imprisonment up to three years for relatively large evasion; imprisonment of three to seven years applies to evasions of a huge amount accounting for more than 30% of the tax due.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is a paper entity with no real people, offices, or substantive AI BPO operations, created to access treaty-reduced dividend withholding rates and pass profits with minimal Chinese substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits and recharacterisation by tax authorities under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule in the Enterprise Income Tax Law and its Implementing Regulations; re-assessed tax, interest, and a penalty up to 50%-500% of any underpayments. The beneficial ownership test under Announcement 60/2015 and the substance-over-form doctrine nullify the structural tax advantage.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil where willful evasion is established; directors are individually liable for the shortfall, may be travel-banned and placed on the public joint credit blacklist, and may face criminal tax evasion liability with imprisonment up to seven years for significant amounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Foreign Exchange Control Violation in Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE routes cross-border payments through PayPal or Wise without declaring the revenue and intercompany services to the tax and foreign exchange authorities, circumventing SAFE current-account verification and withholding obligations, and obscuring beneficial ownership of the underlying BPO profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Foreign exchange regulators may impose fines of 30%-100% of the illegal amount under the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations, tax authorities may disallow deductions and impose withholding penalties for undeclared outbound payments, and anti-money laundering regulators may impose fines on the entity and responsible persons under the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal fines, blacklisting and bank account controls, travel bans while proceedings are pending, and criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 191 for money laundering with prison terms up to five years for the basic offense and longer for serious circumstances, plus civil asset restitution for amounts concealed.
